outcome: No proof, refutation, or partial resolution of this infinitude-of-primes question was found since 26 January 2024; it remains an open conjecture in the Bunyakovsky/Dickson/Schinzel-Hypothesis-H family, with only unrelated computational finds (new large probable/proven generalized-repunit-style primes) occurring in the window.
summary: This bullet is the generalized-repunit-style primality conjecture from the family of Bunyakovsky's conjecture / Dickson's conjecture / Schinzel's Hypothesis H: for fixed k≥1, b≥2, c≠0 with the stated gcd conditions, are there infinitely many n such that (k·b^n+c)/gcd(k+c,b-1) is prime? No case of this general family (beyond Dirichlet's theorem for degree-1 polynomials, which this is not) has ever been proved, and I found no claimed progress, partial resolution, or refutation dated in the 26 Jan 2024–22 Sep 2026 window. Searches for the exact expression, for 'generalized repunit prime conjecture', and for AI-related proof activity in this area returned nothing on point. Two tempting leads turned out to be irrelevant on inspection: (1) a 2025 arXiv/JIS paper by E. Cohen, 'Conjectures about Primes and Cyclic Numbers' (J. Integer Sequences 28 (2025), 25.4.7), which is about a different, unrelated family of 66 conjectures concerning cyclic numbers and Sophie Germain primes — not this conjecture — and one of whose sub-conjectures (a subadditivity conjecture, #66) was refuted by a human (Josué Alexander Ibarra) with a Lean-verified counterexample; (2) a November 2025 arXiv paper, 'Mathematics with large language models as provers and verifiers' (arXiv:2510.12829), reporting a GPT-5-based prover/verifier system that closed 22 of that same 66-conjecture list (17 proofs, 5 refutations) — but again this is the Cohen cyclic-number/Sophie-Germain list, not the generalized-repunit conjecture on our bullet, and I could not find our specific expression anywhere in that paper's Table 3 conjecture list. The only concrete events in the window relating to generalized repunit-style primes were computational discoveries — e.g. the repunit R(109297) being proven prime by elliptic-curve primality proving around May 2025 (t5k.org) — but per §3.1 a new record instance or verified-to-a-larger-limit search does not advance an 'are there infinitely many' question, so this does not change the status. No AI involvement of any kind was found in connection with this specific conjecture.
competing_reading: One could argue that any progress on the broader Bunyakovsky conjecture, Dickson's conjecture, or Schinzel's Hypothesis H (of which this is a special/derived case) should count as 'progress' on this bullet under a generous reading of scope. I did not find any such progress in the window either (these remain fully open apart from Dirichlet's theorem, which predates the window by centuries), so this does not change the classification, but if any such general progress exists and I missed it, this record would need revision to `progress` rather than `open`.
what_would_settle_it: A preprint or announcement that either proves infinitude of primes for some fixed (k,b,c) instance of this family, proves a positive-density/lower-bound result specific to this parametrized form, or explicitly references this generalized-repunit primality conjecture (e.g. citing Guy's 'Unsolved Problems in Number Theory' or the Wikipedia bullet) with a claimed resolution.
